takeaway: Young patient with an intracapsular femoral neck fracture: cannulated screws, preserving the femoral head, because femoral head prostheses have a limited lifespan.

lines.text: A thirty-five-year-old woman is hit by a car.
Her plain X-ray shows an intracapsular fracture of the right femoral neck.
In younger patients with intracapsular fractures, cannulated screws are preferred.
They fix the fracture and preserve the head of the femur.
A replacement head is avoided, because femoral head prostheses have a limited lifespan.
So for this young woman, the operation is cannulated screws.
